title: LID Chicken & Ginger Tinola Broth
ingredients: 1 lb fresh chicken cutlets, cut into pieces
2 inches fresh ginger, sliced into thin coins
instructions: Heat pure canola oil in a heavy soup pot over medium heat. Sauté fresh ginger coins, chopped onion, and minced garlic for 2–3 minutes until aromatic.
Add fresh chicken cutlets and sear lightly for 4–5 minutes until the exterior turns white.
Pour in 4 cups of filtered water. Bring to a rolling boil, skim any surface foam, then lower heat to a gentle simmer for 20 minutes.
Add peeled sliced sayote (chayote) and simmer for an additional 5–7 minutes until tender yet crisp.
Season with pure non-iodized kosher salt and cracked black pepper to taste. Ladle hot broth over steamed white jasmine rice.
clinicalNote: Traditional comfort soup adapted for RAI: uses sayote as a safe potato substitute, completely eliminates commercial chicken bouillon cubes and fish sauce (patis), and seasons exclusively with verified non-iodized kosher salt.

title: Pan-Seared Garlic Olive Oil Steak
ingredients: 8 oz fresh beef sirloin or ribeye steak cut (unbrined)
1 cup fresh green beans, trimmed (or zucchini slices)
1 cup steamed jasmine white rice (cooked in filtered water)
instructions: Pat fresh beef steak dry on all sides using paper towels. Generously rub with 1 tbsp olive oil, minced garlic, pure non-iodized kosher salt, and coarse black pepper.
Heat a heavy cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until hot. Add steak and sear undisturbed for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Transfer steak to a cutting board and allow to rest for 5 minutes so juices redistribute.
In the same skillet with pan drippings, toss trimmed green beans with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of non-iodized kosher salt for 3–4 minutes until blistered and tender-crisp.
Slice steak against the grain and serve alongside sautéed green beans and freshly steamed jasmine white rice.
clinicalNote: Fresh unbrined beef provides high-quality protein without the commercial tenderizers, marinades, soy sauce (toyo), or iodized salt ubiquitous in restaurant steaks.

title: Crispy Pork Chops with Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges
ingredients: 2 fresh bone-in pork chops (unbrined, approx. 1 inch thick)
2 medium sweet potatoes, thoroughly peeled and cut into 1/2-inch wedges
2 tbsp pure extra virgin olive oil
1 tsp pure garlic powder (single ingredient, no added salt)
1 tsp pure onion powder (single ingredient, no added salt)
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Thoroughly peel sweet potatoes (peeling removes skin mineral density). Toss wedges with 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, and 1/2 tsp non-iodized kosher salt.
Spread wedges in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25 minutes, flipping once halfway, until edges are caramelized and crispy.
Pat pork chops dry. Rub with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and 1/2 tsp non-iodized kosher salt.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork chops for 5–6 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F). Serve with roasted sweet potato wedges.
clinicalNote: Sweet potatoes are a permitted root vegetable rich in vitamins A and C. Pure single-origin spices deliver robust savory flavor without relying on dairy butter rubs or commercial spice blends containing hidden sea salt.

title: Fresh Fruit & Cinnamon Rolled Oats
ingredients: 1 cup plain rolled oats (unfortified, 100% whole grain)
1 fresh crisp apple, cored and diced
1 tbsp 100% pure maple syrup or raw honey
instructions: In a small saucepan, bring 2 cups of filtered water and a tiny pinch of pure non-iodized kosher salt to a gentle boil.
Stir in rolled oats. Lower heat to medium-low and simmer for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally until thick and creamy.
Pour hot oatmeal into a serving bowl.
Top with diced fresh apple and sliced fresh banana.
Drizzle with 100% pure maple syrup or raw honey and dust with pure ground cinnamon before serving.
clinicalNote: Safe, nourishing alternative to commercial boxed breakfast cereals (which often contain dairy whey or iodized salt) and commercial bakery breads (frequently made with potassium iodate dough conditioners).

title: Egg White & Avocado Breakfast Bowl
ingredients: 3 large fresh egg whites (meticulously separated from yolks)
1 medium ripe tomato, sliced into rounds
1 tsp 100% pure olive oil or canola oil
1 tbsp fresh scallions or cilantro, finely chopped
instructions: Carefully separate egg whites from yolks, ensuring zero yolk enters the bowl (discard yolks or reserve for family members not on LID).
Whisk egg whites with a pinch of non-iodized kosher salt and cracked black pepper until frothy.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat. Pour in egg whites and gently scramble with a spatula for 2–3 minutes until just set and fluffy.
Transfer warm scrambled egg whites to a shallow bowl.
Arrange sliced fresh avocado and ripe tomato rounds adjacent to the eggs.
Season avocado and tomatoes with remaining pure non-iodized kosher salt and garnish with fresh scallions or cilantro.
clinicalNote: Commercial chicken feed fortifies egg yolks with 12–25 mcg of iodine each. Pure egg whites (albumen) are virtually iodine-free. Fresh avocado provides healthy monounsaturated fats in place of dairy butter.

title: Herb-Roasted Chicken Breast with Steamed Broccoli
ingredients: 2 fresh boneless, skinless chicken breasts (unbrined, approx. 12 oz total)
2 cups fresh broccoli florets, steamed in filtered water
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Lightly oil a baking dish with olive oil.
In a small ramekin, whisk 1.5 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried rosemary, dried thyme, 1 tsp non-iodized kosher salt, and black pepper.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Coat both sides thoroughly with the garlic-herb marinade.
Place chicken breasts in the baking dish and bake for 22–25 minutes until internal temperature registers 74°C (165°F). Let rest 5 minutes before slicing.
While chicken rests, steam broccoli florets over boiling filtered water for 4–5 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Toss with remaining 1/2 tbsp olive oil.
Serve sliced roasted chicken breast over steamed broccoli with a spoonful of aromatic pan juices.
clinicalNote: Eliminates store-bought rotisserie poultry and commercial frozen meats injected with iodized salt solutions. Fresh lemon juice and dried herbs provide bright, savory depth with zero added sodium or dairy.

title: Homemade Roasted Tomato & Basil Soup
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh ripe Roma tomatoes, halved lengthwise
1 large yellow onion, sliced into wedges
6 cloves fresh garlic, peeled and smashed
2 tbsp pure extra virgin olive oil
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, washed and loosely torn
1 tsp pure cane sugar or raw honey
instructions: Preheat oven to 205°C (400°F). Arrange halved tomatoes, onion wedges, and smashed garlic cloves on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Drizzle vegetables with 2 tbsp olive oil and season with 1/2 tsp non-iodized kosher salt and cracked black pepper.
Roast in the oven for 30 minutes until tomatoes are slightly charred and garlic is golden and soft.
Transfer all roasted vegetables and pan juices into a medium soup pot. Add 2 cups filtered water and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Add fresh basil leaves, then blend using an immersion stick blender until velvety smooth.
Stir in 1 tsp pure sugar (or honey) and remaining 1/2 tsp pure non-iodized kosher salt to balance acidity. Serve steaming hot.
clinicalNote: Commercial canned tomato soups and pasta sauces ubiquitously contain iodized canning salt, dairy milk, cream, and preservatives. This homemade recipe uses 100% fresh produce and pure olive oil for clean, safe comfort.

title: Crispy Baked Potato Fries (Peeled)
ingredients: 2 large russet potatoes, completely peeled and cut into 1/4-inch fries
2 tbsp pure extra virgin olive oil
1/2 tsp pure garlic powder (no added salt)
instructions: Thoroughly peel the potatoes, making sure all skin and eyes are completely removed (potato skin concentrates soil minerals and iodine; peeling is mandatory on LID).
Cut peeled potatoes into uniform 1/4-inch matchsticks. Submerge matchsticks in a bowl of cold filtered water for 30 minutes to draw out excess surface starch.
Drain potatoes thoroughly and pat completely dry using clean kitchen towels or paper towels (dry fries crisp better).
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). In a large bowl, toss dry potato fries with olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, non-iodized kosher salt, and black pepper.
Arrange in a single layer without overlapping on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake for 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until crisp and golden brown.
clinicalNote: Commercial fast-food french fries and frozen potato brands use iodized salt and beef-derived dairy flavorings. Soaking and thoroughly peeling fresh potatoes minimizes soil iodine, creating a safe, satisfying crunch.

title: Simple Lemon-Garlic Sautéed Pork Cutlets with White Rice
ingredients: 1 lb fresh raw pork loin cutlets, sliced thin (unseasoned, unbrined)
2 cups freshly steamed jasmine white rice (cooked in filtered water)
instructions: Season thin pork loin cutlets on both sides with pure non-iodized kosher salt, black pepper, and dried oregano.
Heat 1 tbsp pure canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add pork cutlets in a single layer and sear for 2–3 minutes per side until nicely browned.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add minced garlic and fresh lemon juice to the skillet, swirling the pan for 1–2 minutes to create a light pan glaze that coats the cutlets.
Remove from heat immediately to preserve tenderness. Spoon warm pan sauce over the pork cutlets and serve alongside steamed white rice.
clinicalNote: Fresh lemon juice and garlic provide tangy savory flavor without needing soy sauce (toyo), oyster sauce, or Worcestershire sauce (which contain anchovies, soy, and iodized sea salt).

title: Apple Cinnamon Compote with Raw Walnuts
ingredients: 2 large fresh crisp apples (Fuji or Gala), peeled, cored, and diced
1 tbsp pure brown sugar or raw honey
1/4 tsp pure vanilla extract (100% pure, no artificial additives)
1/4 cup raw unsalted walnuts, roughly chopped
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine diced apples, filtered water, pure brown sugar (or raw honey), ground cinnamon, and a tiny pinch of non-iodized kosher salt.
Cover with a lid and simmer over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until apples soften and liquid reduces to a warm syrup.
Remove saucepan from heat and gently fold in pure vanilla extract.
In a dry skillet over low heat, lightly toast the raw walnuts for 2–3 minutes until fragrant. Confirm walnuts are 100% raw and unsalted before toasting.
Divide warm apple compote into small dessert bowls, top with toasted walnuts, and serve warm or chilled.
clinicalNote: Satisfies dessert cravings without commercial baked pastries (which use iodate dough conditioners and butter). Uses raw unsalted walnuts, avoiding commercial roasted nut mixes that are salted with iodized table salt.
